The '申' glyph cue borrows from the Japanese bureaucratic-window tradition and the modern paperwork-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as submit-coded rather than literal monkey (the radical's other meaning).

In real-world usage 🈸 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate paperwork energy. A partner sends it on a 'ideographic-application-coded 🈸' form check-in.
